name: number-input
summary: A number between a lowest and a highest value, inside its field: ArrowUp and ArrowDown step it and stop at either end, a step button on each side disables at its bound, and its label scrubs it, with read-only, disabled and invalid.

notCovered.name: a pressed step button
notCovered.why: A press on an enabled step button steps the value: a mouse press at once, with focus put in the input, and a touch press when it ends or while it is held. A pressed look the check drives would change the value as it reads it, so the button has none of its own: held down it draws as it does at rest, or under a mouse as it does under the pointer, and the live buttons and a pinned row show both. A disabled button takes no press, and in the read-only field the buttons take no pointer.

notCovered.name: a focused step button
notCovered.why: UI SDK keeps both step buttons out of the Tab order. A mouse press on an enabled one puts focus in the input, a touch press leaves focus where it was, a disabled one takes no focus, and in the read-only field the buttons take no pointer, so no step button ever holds focus or draws the focus ring; the arrow keys give the same steps from the input.

notCovered.name: ui-number-input-scrub-area-cursor
notCovered.why: UI SDK moves the scrub cursor to the body and places it there in its style attribute while a drag holds the pointer, which the check refuses on a stage, so the stage holds none. Where the browser grants pointer lock during a drag on the label, the pointer is hidden and nothing stands in for it until the drag ends.

notCovered.name: a drag on the label
notCovered.why: The check does not drag; a drag changes the value as the arrow keys do, and the part gives data-scrubbing no look of its own, so the stage draws as it does at rest while the value moves.

notCovered.name: the selected value
notCovered.why: A click on the label that does not drag puts focus in the input and selects its value; the browser draws the selection in its own colours, which no skin variable sets and the check does not read, and the part sets none.

notCovered.name: the touch target
notCovered.why: Under a coarse pointer UI SDK lays an empty box over each step button, 2.75rem tall, so a tap near it reaches it. It draws nothing, so no light reads its size, and the part leaves it as UI SDK sets it.

notCovered.name: the mouse wheel
notCovered.why: UI SDK steps a focused number input by the wheel only when it sets wheel; no number input here sets it, so the wheel scrolls the page.
